meta.action: Check whether the answer is supported by a retrieved chunk. If not, treat it as a customer-facing error.

values.description: Correct chunk retrieved but model refused due to context noise or multi-part query sensitivity.

values.label: Corpus Gap
values.description: The answer simply does not exist in any indexed document. Retrieval cannot fix this: new content must be authored.

values.label: Citation Abbreviation
values.description: Model produced a correct answer but shortened chunk IDs; exact-match validator rejects abbreviated IDs.

values.label: Citation Character Error
values.description: Model used an en-dash (U+2013) instead of a double hyphen as the chunk ID separator; one character breaks validation.

values.label: Corpus Gap / False Refusal
values.description: Model refused: either the document is missing from the corpus entirely, or context noise caused an unnecessary refusal.

values.label: Multi-turn conversations. Every case is a single ticket; a customer who replies is not simulated (see the bonus second-contact eval).
Real re-open behaviour. Deflection here means 'answered correctly by our assertions', not 'the customer did not write back'.
Real help-centre language. The corpus and tickets are SYNTHETIC and templated, so retrieval scores are optimistic compared with real articles.
Languages other than English, attachments, screenshots, voice.
Account data errors. The entitlement tool is assumed correct; a wrong plan in the account system produces a confidently wrong answer.
Adversarial inputs beyond two injection cases; one of them is caught by a regex before any model runs.
Load. Latency and cost are measured one ticket at a time; concurrency is only modelled in the 10x plan.
Tone and brand voice beyond the judge's one-line rubric.
